note: The shared access-state contract (#77). Every SDK runs every case and must agree, because these are the states that decide whether a paying customer keeps working. A harness starts a clock at T0, mints and stores a signed token if `token` is set, sets the revoked marker if `revoked` is true, then walks `steps`: each step moves the clock by that many seconds and evaluates open() with the network down. The last verdict must equal `expect`. Copied verbatim into every SDK repo; the copies are checked byte for byte.

cases.name: first run with nothing stored asks for a key, and never says revoked
a revocation we were actually told about survives the token being erased
a fresh token unlocks with no network at all
past the token lifetime but inside the licence is grace, never a lockout
a perpetual licence keeps working however long the app is offline
a signed expiry that has passed ends access offline
a trial gets no grace past its token, or a blocked endpoint is a free licence
a trial inside its token unlocks like anything else
a token that says disabled is a revocation we are holding in our hand
winding the clock back keeps access and says so
winding the clock back cannot resurrect a licence that ended
capabilities come off the signed token with no call
a licence with no capabilities reports none rather than an empty set
